limits: No alternative runtime was executed or benchmarked in this slice; no measured latency, memory or runtime superiority claim.
No MLS/CNSA, installed-product, hardware, availability or whole-lane qualification.
component: Immutable evidence byte binding and returned digest/expiry metadata
constraints: Offline exact tuple of 1..16 immutable bytes values, each at most 65536 bytes; complete pre-validation before signature or content hashing.
Authenticate the same envelope/policy snapshot, match every signed digest and preserve signed order/kind/outcome. Return metadata only, never qualification or motion authority.
No specified target hardware or hard deadline; bounds describe input bytes, not total memory or completion time.
alternatives: Python exact bytes/tuple and native-backed hashlib composed with the versioned verifier.
Rust immutable borrows with RustCrypto SHA-2 and an independently conformant verifier adapter.
Erlang/Elixir immutable binaries with OTP crypto hash and a strict verifier adapter.
C#/F# SHA256.HashData with owned immutable snapshot semantics; read-only views alone do not prevent mutation through another alias.
rationale: KEEP the runtime after fresh source and contract review: immutable values preserve the authenticated snapshot across digest checks without a second trust-policy implementation. Each candidate can hash bytes; no material improvement to the required semantics is demonstrated by changing the implementation boundary.

FIX standalone assurance: the eleven existing evidence methods survived independently removed output digest and policy expiry cap. Two added real-signature methods now reject those changes; production runtime is unchanged.
